title: Performance comparison of retrieval-augmented generation and fine-tuned large language models for construction safety management knowledge retrieval
summary: Construction safety standards are in unstructured formats like text and images, complicating their effective use in daily tasks. This paper compares the performance of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and fine-tuned Large Language Model (LLM) for the construction safety knowledge retrieval. The RAG model was created by integrating GPT-4 with a knowledge graph derived from construction safety guidelines, while the fine-tuned LLM was fine-tuned using a question-answering dataset derived from the same guidelines.

title: Deep learning for post-hurricane aerial damage assessment of buildings
summary: This study aims to improve post-disaster preliminary damage assessment (PDA) using artificial intelligence (AI) and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery. To account for the ordinality of damage level classes, the cross-entropy classification loss function is replaced with the square of earth mover's distance (EMD2) loss. summary: This paper presents a framework for interactive and traceable visual bridge inspections by integrating AI-driven image processing models with extended reality. title: PyStruct3D: Bounding box fitting and reconstruction for scan-to-BIM workflows
summary: PyStruct3D is an open-source Python library supporting scan-to-BIM workflows as part of the BIMStruct3D pipeline. It provides tools for fitting bounding geometry to segmented point cloud instances, evaluating reconstruction accuracy, and visualizing 3D structural elements. Built on NumPy, SciPy, and Open3D, it helps researchers and developers streamline structural reconstruction from point cloud data.

title: CrisiSense-RAG: Crisis Sensing Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Rapid Disaster Impact Assessment
summary: Timely and spatially resolved disaster impact assessment is essential for effective emergency response. However, automated methods typically struggle with temporal asynchrony. Real-time human reports capture peak hazard conditions, while high-resolution satellite imagery is frequently acquired after peak conditions. This often reflects flood recession rather than the maximum extent. Naive fusion of these misaligned streams can yield dangerous underestimates when post-event imagery overrides documented peak flooding

field_text.description: Construction worker human activity recognition on VTT-ConIoT using both 6-class grouped activities and 16-class fine-grained activities. The canonical benchmark results use 5 s windows and report LOSO mean accuracy and standard deviation across 13 participants. VTT-ConIoT contains wearable IMU data from 13 participants performing 16 construction-related activities using three sensor locations (hip, back, and shoulder). The paper evaluates human activity recognition with six machine-learning classifiers using LOSO validation. Tables 2–3 use 5 s windows. In the paper's window-size analysis, the best 6-class accuracy increases to 0.94 and the best 16-class accuracy increases to 0.84 with 10 s windows using all sensors/signals.

title: CMOT: Construction Multi-Object Tracking
summary: Construction-specific multi-object tracking benchmark across ten worker, precast-component, truck, and heavy-machinery categories. The benchmark compares SORT, DeepSORT, StrongSORT, two prior construction trackers, and the proposed MOT method under three instance-segmentation backbone detectors.
metrics: Overall tracking performance across all CMOT object categories, reported in Table 8 of Yan et al. (2025).

field_text.identity: cmot-multi-object-tracking-results CMOT: Construction Multi-Object Tracking multi-object-tracking CMOT Construction Multiobject Tracking (CMOT) Dataset
field_text.description: Construction-specific multi-object tracking benchmark across ten worker, precast-component, truck, and heavy-machinery categories. The benchmark compares SORT, DeepSORT, StrongSORT, two prior construction trackers, and the proposed MOT method under three instance-segmentation backbone detectors. CMOT is a construction-specific multi-object tracking dataset containing 100 onsite videos and 155,774 annotations collected through a monitoring platform covering more than 70 construction sites. It includes ten categories: people-helmet, people-no-helmet, precast component (PC), PC-truck, dump-truck, mixer truck, excavator, roller, dozer, and wheel-loader. id: AI Optimizes Building HVAC Energy Use in Berlin
title: AI Optimizes Building HVAC Energy Use in Berlin
summary: At the Treptower office complex in Berlin, an AI-driven HVAC control system (DABBEL AI) autonomously managed heating and cooling. By learning from real-time sensor, occupancy, and weather data, it cut HVAC energy consumption by 36%, saving ~1.76 GWh and 605 tons CO2 annually, which equated to over €180,000 saved in 2023.

title: FAIR Principles
summary: Design datasets so people and machines can discover, access, combine, and reuse them. FAIR raises the baseline for quality by requiring persistent identifiers, rich metadata, interoperable formats, and explicit reuse conditions.

field_text.identity: FAIR Principles
field_text.description: Design datasets so people and machines can discover, access, combine, and reuse them. FAIR raises the baseline for quality by requiring persistent identifiers, rich metadata, interoperable formats, and explicit reuse conditions. Findable · Accessible · Interoperable · Reusable Any dataset release (internal or public) that should be citable and maintainable. Collaborations where multiple teams need consistent metadata and formats. Assign a persistent identifier (DOI) and publish a machine-readable metadata record. Use open, standard formats (CSV/JSON, GeoTIFF, LAS/LAZ, E57). Provide a clear license and provenance: who collected, when, where, how; include contact. Create a README and a metadata file; validate with an internal FAIR checklist. Archive a versioned snapshot in a DOI-minting repository (e.g., Zenodo). Cross-link the DOI in papers, model cards, and project pages.
field_text.domain: Core Data Principles

title: TOP Guidelines
summary: Raise trust and reproducibility by openly sharing data, code, and research materials whenever possible. Include a short transparency statement with every publication or release.

field_text.identity: TOP Guidelines
field_text.description: Raise trust and reproducibility by openly sharing data, code, and research materials whenever possible. Include a short transparency statement with every publication or release. Transparency and Openness Promotion Publications and technical reports that rely on datasets and code. Benchmarks and leaderboards where comparability matters. State where the data and code are available, under what license, and how to access them. Document provenance, known limits, and evaluation protocols to avoid misuse. Encourage preregistration when appropriate (e.g., planned evaluation criteria). Add a transparency statement with links to datasets, code, and documentation. Share evaluation scripts and configs so others can reproduce metrics.
field_text.domain: Transparency
